title: Cisco Catalyst Center Devices and Interfaces
description: Drill-down companion to the Cisco Catalyst Center Overview dashboard: device health and resources, interface status and errors, throughput and uplinks, and opt-in switch stack, PoE, and AP radio health.

definition.content:
## Cisco Catalyst Center

This drill-down companion to the [Cisco Catalyst Center Overview](/dash/integration/Cisco%20Catalyst%20Center%20Overview) dashboard shows which devices are unhealthy or short on resources, which interfaces are down or erroring, and where throughput goes, especially on uplinks. The stack, PoE, and AP radio groups stay empty until their collectors are enabled.

**Filters:** `catalyst_center_host` and `device_ip` scope every widget. `site_hierarchy` also narrows device and interface widgets, except the per-device throughput and uplink rollups and the stack widgets. `device_family` narrows device and AP radio widgets only.

**Useful links**
- [Integration docs](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/cisco_catalyst_center/)
- [Integration tile](/integrations/cisco-catalyst-center)
- [Cisco Catalyst Center](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/products/networking/catalyst-center/index.html)

Health is Catalyst Center's composite score from 1 to 10: 8 to 10 is good, 4 to 7 fair, and 1 to 3 poor. Start with the lowest health, then check the component scores to see what pulls it down. A blank cell means no value was reported, not zero.
Top 10 devices per chart. Dashed lines mark the 70% warning and 80% critical levels; temperature limits vary by platform.
Clients connected to each device, split into wired and wireless. A sudden drop on one device usually points to a problem on that device or its uplink.

Catalyst Center's own count of affected interfaces on each device. Inter-device links connect network devices to each other, so treat any that are down as urgent. WAN link utilization fills in only for devices that report a WAN link.
1 is up and 0 is down. Admin down means shut on purpose; down with admin up is unexpected, though unused access ports report it too.
Values are percentages of packets, not counts. Errors usually mean cabling, optics, or duplex faults; discards usually mean congestion.
Throughput is in bits per second, and device totals sum each device's interfaces. Utilization is the share of an interface's negotiated speed; sustained values above 80% risk congestion and discards.
Uplinks are interfaces Catalyst Center flags as WAN links or, where it does not say, whose description contains "uplink". Devices with neither report no uplinks and stay out of these widgets.
Wireless controllers only. Free timer and free memory buffer are the percentage still available, so falling values mean less headroom.
Scores from 1 to 10 across each device's radios. Low scores point to RF noise, interference, poor air quality, or busy channels.
Opt-in: empty until `collect_stacks: true` is set, and only switches are polled. Ready and in sync report 1; anything else reports 0.
Opt-in: empty until `collect_interface_poe: true` is set, and always empty on hardware without PoE. Values are in watts.

Opt-in: empty until `collect_wireless: true` is set. Channel utilization is total airtime in use and Wi-Fi traffic utilization the part carrying Wi-Fi frames. Noise is in dBm, where more negative is quieter.
